newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank Byblos shareholders okay capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Bank Byblos shareholders okay capital increase.

text.p: Shareholders at Lebanon's Byblos bank approved a share capital increase to 204 billion Lebanese pounds ($132 million) from 66 billion pounds, the bank said on Tuesday.

"On June 9,1997, Bank Byblos shareholders held an extraordinary session...and it was decided to increase the bank's capital from 66 billion pounds to 204 billion Lebanese pounds," the bank said in a statement.
"The board of directors was delegated to set the invitation date and the terms of the increase," it added.
The bank said the increase, expected to be carried out before the end of September, "would be followed by listing the bank shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange".
Byblos is one of Lebanon's most dynamic banks and its listing is eagerly awaited on the re-emerging Beirut bourse. Its shares have quadrupled on the parallel market in the past two years.

Byblos' listing on the exchange was originally intended for the beginning of the year but was delayed due to the need to meet a legal requirement that 33 percent of its shares remain in Lebanese hands after listing.

In order to meet this requirement, Byblos is creating a new Lebanese-based holding company. This will be 50 percent owned by Lebanese who will hold 30 percent of the bank's A shares -- restricted to Lebanese citizens, a bank official said earlier.

The latest increase is part of the bank's programme to raise its capitalisation to $200 million whithin 18 months as announced by Chairman Francois Bassile at the beginning of the year, the bank's statement said.
